the-rejection-evidence-contract-released.text: The rejection evidence contract released to the validator and builder tickets.

This page is the contract that ticket 495 (validators) and ticket 496 (off-chain evidence and builders) consume. It states what the model proves and what an implementation must establish to correspond to it. It is written at the model's level: it fixes facts and their order, not byte encodings, redeemer layouts or fees, which the consuming tickets choose and must show correspond.

standing-since-14-october-2026.text: This page is the contract of the first stage of the ticket: a rejection that carries evidence inside the transaction of a fold, and the mixed batch of folds and rejections. The model keeps that stage as a named legacy path, so the page stays true of it. It is not the contract for the ruled economics: a rejection now reads the current state by reference, spends no state output and never shares a transaction with a fold, and refunds are summed per refund address. The economic contract is the contract for booking, rejection, retraction and the fold, and the release record names the model revision.

story.text: As the author of a validator, I read what a rejection must prove, in what order a refusal is named, what a batch binds, and what the model deliberately leaves to me, so that a transaction built by someone who bypasses every command line is still refused unless it satisfies the rule.

what-a-rejection-must-carry.text: A rejection of a pending request is admitted only when the transaction presents all of the following, and each is checked against the state the rejection is judged on.

A mismatch names the leaf the key holds. It is admitted exactly when that leaf is the leaf held at the key under the judged root and the request's edge has no successor from it. The unknown leaf, a non-membership proof, and the stored Absent state are different leaves: a request to insert is compatible at unknown and mismatched at Absent, Active and Terminal; a request to terminate is compatible at Active and mismatched elsewhere. A request naming an excluded edge tag (ruled by the epic owner as an application of the first ruling, see the decisions page) is mismatched at every leaf.
An expiry is admitted exactly when the interval's lower bound is at or after the request's booked time plus the configuration's processing duration plus its reclaim duration.

the-order-refusals-are-named.text: The model names the first failing check in this order: evidence missing; the registry (identity, configuration or root); the request; the interval; then the ground (leaf mismatch, compatible, not expired). An implementation may refuse for a different reason in a different order only if it refuses exactly the same set of rejections; the conformance rows compare the reason the chain reports with the model's, so ticket 495 should keep this order unless it escalates.

what-the-proof-must-establish.text: The model's evidence is a logical read of the registry, not proof bytes. A concrete verifier corresponds to the model only if a proof that verifies establishes exactly the leaf the evidence names against the root the rejection is judged on. A proof that fails to verify, a provider that fails to answer, an input the processor omitted and a script that fails for any reason are not evidence of a lifecycle mismatch and never admit a rejection.

what-a-rejection-does.text: An admitted rejection leaves the registry state exactly as the judged state, mints nothing, requires no signer, and owes the owner the deposit it owed before this contract existed: through the same payment, with the same floors. The refund policy of ticket 361 is untouched. The tip is not a payment of the rejection; the model states no routing of the tip.

what-a-batch-binds.text: Each action is judged on the state the actions before it left, and a rejection's evidence binds that intermediate state's configuration and root, never the root the transaction started from. A rejection leaves its state unchanged, so later actions see every earlier fold. The first refused action refuses the whole batch with its own reason and leaves no partial result. An empty batch is refused. All actions share one validity interval. A foldable request cannot be rejected at any position of an admitted batch.

what-the-model-leaves-to-the-consuming-t.text: What the model leaves to the consuming tickets.

The byte encoding of evidence and of the batch, the redeemer layout, the proof format and its verifier, how a processor finds the pending requests, fees, the routing of the tip, the request tag and its bond (ticket 529), and whether and how a rejection is its own command (ticket 487). None of them may weaken the rows above; each must show correspondence.

release-record.text: The release is the merge commit of ticket 494's pull request. Its record, with the model revision, the digest of each statement, the corpus rows, the constitution version and the limits that remain, is the release record.
